title: GitHub Copilot Fusion adds experimental routing between local and cloud models
dek: Supported on-device models can join Copilot's routing pool, but cloud-based routing decisions mean the workflow is not offline.
evidence: GitHub product preview documentation; no independent local-versus-cloud performance benchmark
takeaway: On-device inference is not the same as offline operation. Cloud routing can remain in the control path even when generation happens locally.

sections.title: What's new

bullets.detail: Copilot can download and configure MAI Code 1.1 Flash through Windows ML on supported Windows hardware. The feature is opt-in and uses Fusion Standard for automatic local/cloud routing.
Copilot CLI can route to supported manually configured local models on Windows, macOS and Linux through an OpenAI-compatible server. GitHub names MAI Code 1.1 Flash and Qwen3.8 Flash Next.

The Copilot app can select compatible local models directly, but automatic routing there currently supports managed Windows ML models only. Adding a BYOK model does not automatically make it eligible for Fusion routing.

sections.title: Evidence & limitations

bullets.detail: GitHub labels the feature experimental and does not report a controlled task-success, token-cost, energy-use or latency comparison between routed local and cloud execution.
GitHub explicitly says Copilot Fusion still makes routing decisions in the cloud. Local model execution does not establish that prompts, metadata or control-plane traffic remain on the device.
Local models can have different safety protections from Copilot's hosted models; the device also needs enough compute and memory for the selected runtime.

sections.title: Key takeaways

bullets.detail: A model can generate tokens on-device while a remote service still selects the model or coordinates execution.
Local generation reduces some remote processing, but privacy depends on which task data and metadata cross the network boundary.

paragraphs: Compute and control are separate: A model can generate tokens on-device while a remote service still selects the model or coordinates execution.
